newsitem.title: GERMANY: Audi confirms considering building US plant.
newsitem.headline: Audi confirms considering building US plant.

text.p: Audi AG, the luxury carmaker unit of Volkswagen AG, confirmed a published report on Wednesday saying it was studying the feasibility of building a production plant in the United States.

The Wall Street Journal Europe said Audi was reviewing plans for a major production plant to begin operations sometime after the year 2000 amid early evidence that it was narrowing a site search to five states in the U.S. Southeast.

"We are doing a survey in America as we do in many other countries around the world to see whether it makes sense to be an importer or to build up production in some form," Audi spokesman Norbert Essing told Reuters.
But Essing said, "It is far from anything that may look like a decision. We are far away from anything that might even have a little bit of a character of a decision."

The five U.S. states under consideration are Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia. Rival carmaker BMW AG has a plant in South Carolina and Mercedes-Benz AG has a plant in Alabama.

The report said Audi was also considering building plants in several other countries. The Audi investment would mark the return to the U.S. for Volkswagen which had produced cars in Pennsylvania for 10 years until 1988.

Audi last year sold about 27,000 vehicles in the United States, a 51 percent increase in sales over 1995, but has long said it would need to sell at least 50,000 vehicles to justify a plant in the U.S.
Audi and VW currently import vehicles to the U.S. from Germany and Mexico.
